messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: spike detected in policy-engine evaluation errors -> smart-routing fallbacks. 5xx traces + increased p95 latency in multiple regions. Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/ops/alerts/1839995555

 taylor (oncall): ack. paging @sam, @maria. I'm on it. starting triage — collecting logs and impact windows.

 ops-bot: Attached sample eval log (first 3 errors):
```
2026-11-12T14:12:33Z ERROR policy_engine: eval panic: invalid expression at token '::' (policy_id=route_23)
stack: runtime panic: invalid expr
  at policy/eval.go:142
  at router/rules.go:87
request_id=abc-123 region=us-east-1 fallback=compact-model-v1
```

 sam (sre): on call. seeing elevated fallback rate -> regional routing loop? can you confirm if traffic is repeatedly hitting fallback variant or flapping across regions? need time series on fallbacks and upstream model responses.

 ops-bot: Time window 14:10-14:18: fallback rate per-region:
- us-east-1: 18% -> 65% within 4m
- eu-west-1: 5% -> 40%
- ap-south-1: 2% -> 12%
Full graph: https://redwood.internal/metrics/policy/fallbacks?window=8m

 taylor (oncall): pattern: a recently-updated smart-routing policy (route_23) started throwing eval panics, causing smart-router to treat it as ineligible and return fallback routing. Because fallback variant is different across regions, some requests got bounced between regional proxies during retries -> higher latencies and some 5xxs.

 maria (plateng): I deployed a small change to route_23 ~10m ago (PR: https://git.internal/redwood/policies/pulls/942). The change added a new dynamic expression that uses regex groups and the `extract()` helper. pulling the exact expression now.

 ops-bot: policy expression dump for route_23:
```
when: request.user_agent matches /bot:\/v(\d+)::(beta)/ and request.region != "ap-south-1"
then: prefer region("us-east-1")
```
stack trace shows the regex token '::' is not handled by the expression parser -> panic at parse stage.

 sam (sre): that's the smoking gun. parser doesn't escape literal '::' in our grammar; earlier inputs tolerated it but this new pattern triggers a panic path in policy engine.

 taylor (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable smart-routing for route_23 (force static region preference) 2) roll back PR/patch to policy config 3) hotfix policy-engine to return evaluation error instead of panic. I'll apply 1 now.

 (taylor runs command)
```
# apply temporary override to pin route_23 to us-east-1
redwoodctl routing override set --policy route_23 --mode static --region us-east-1 --reason "mitigate panic -> fallback loop"
```

 ops-bot: override applied, TTL 1h.

 dan (customer-success): which customers saw this? any paying accounts hitting SLOs? I'm prepping comms if needed.

 taylor (oncall): early list: atlantic-payments, docucloud, and two smaller test tenants. Atlantics saw p95/latency jump from 220ms -> 900ms and ~3% error spikes during the window. CS impact likely limited to high-volume endpoints.

 sam (sre): after override, fallbacks dropped to baseline within 90s. p95 returning to normal. graphs: https://redwood.internal/metrics/policy/fallbacks?window=20m

 incident-bot: Metrics update: fallback rate overall dropped from 42% -> 6% in 3m. request error rate decreased accordingly.

 maria (plateng): confirming rollback of PR 942 now. rolling out revert to policy catalog; will follow up with a patch to sanitize regex tokens before parsing. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/policies/pulls/943 (revert + input validation).

 sam (sre): runbook notes: we need to ensure policy-engine never panics on user expressions. short-term hotfix: wrap parse/eval with recover() and return structured eval error so router sees a deterministic false/skip rather than panic. I'll open a hotfix PR.

 (taylor posts snippet of proposed hotfix)
```
// guard policy evaluation
func safeEval(expr string, ctx Context) (bool, error) {
  defer func() {
    if r := recover(); r != nil {
      // convert to error, do not crash process
      err = fmt.Errorf("policy-eval-panic: %v", r)
    }
  }()
  return evaluate(expr, ctx)
}
```

 maria (plateng): will add a test for corner-case tokens including '::' and unbalanced groups. also will add lint rule on PRs that touch routing expressions.

 dan (customer-success): I'm drafting an incident note for affected customers. will include mitigation steps and ETA for a permanent fix.

 taylor (oncall): handing off to @sam for the long tail and postmortem. I'm going offline to catch up on pages. full context: override applied, rollback started, metrics stabilizing. runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/policy-engine

 sam (sre): taking over. next steps: 1) merge hotfix (priority->hotfix), 2) revert policy change fully and validate expression linting, 3) coordinate postmortem and customer comms with @dan and @maria. I'll keep the pager open for 2h.

 dan (customer-success): noted. will send prioritized customer emails and tag CSMs for Atlantics and DocuCloud.

 taylor (oncall): :white_check_mark: mitigation effective, handing off. please update this thread with any customer replies or regression.

 incident-bot: Incident state -> mitigated (auto-tag: routing-policy-runtime). Monitoring for 2 hours.

 sam (sre): acknowledged. creating tickets: INF-4021 (hotfix), INF-4022 (policy-lint), INF-4023 (postmortem). tagging oncall rotation for follow-up. :thumbsup:

 maria (plateng): quick note — we should also add telemetry to count parser panics as a metric (policy_parser_panic_count) so we can alert on regressions instead of relying on fallback graphs. filing a follow-up RFC.

 (taylor adds final comment)
:point_down: tl;dr: cause = unhandled token in new regex-based expression -> parser panic -> router treated policy as ineligible -> fallback/region-flapping -> customer latencies and minor SLO hits. mitigation = static override + revert PR + hotfix to prevent panic. postmortem next.
